evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.55, FIRST step (leftmost 'alpha' arrow): the cyclohexene molecular ion opens its ring by allylic (radical-site) alpha-cleavage to the ring-opened distonic ion drawn as an open hexagon with a delocalised allyl cation (curved inner line spanning three carbons, plus '+') at one chain end and a '.' at the other. Book draws 0 arc(s); moves <1,2,3> are curator-supplied hooks required for electron balance - NO electron-pushing arc is drawn on this branch (the page shows only the bracketed [M]+., the 'alpha'-labelled reaction arrow and the ring-opened product). Encoded flow: radical site C2 -> forming pi C2=C3; one electron of the ring sigma C3-C4 -> the same forming pi; the second electron of C3-C4 -> C4 (new primary radical). LOCALIZATION (convention C): the book draws the intact C=C with a bracketed '+.', so this record localises the ionised pi bond as C1(+)/C2(.) - exactly the localisation the MOD retro-Diels-Alder rules use ('[C+]5[C.]6' in IMS_4_31_alpha1 / IMS_4_32_alpha) - and the ring-opened allyl cation as C3=C2-C1(+); the partner resonance form C3(+)-C2=C1 is equally valid and is what the book's delocalised drawing covers. The prose above the scheme states that the ring 'possible a concerted, as well as a stepwise, dissociation of two ring bonds'; the scheme drawn (and encoded here) is the STEPWISE route through this distonic intermediate.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.55; no MOD rule variable is cross-linked to this equation. Nearest encodings: the Ch. 4 retro-Diels-Alder pair IMS_4_31_alpha1 and IMS_4_32_alpha (identical DFS '[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C.]6[C]7{-}2>>[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7'), which encode exactly this ring-opening geometry (radical site 6, new pi 6=7, cleaved ring bond 7-2 incident to the pi-forming atom 7, radical left on 2). VERIFIED MISMATCH FOR THIS SUBSTRATE: their left side needs SEVEN carbons - a six-ring PLUS an exocyclic C (atom 1) on the ring carbon that becomes the radical - so it cannot match unsubstituted cyclohexene (C6H10+., six carbons, no exocyclic C). RDKit substructure test of the rule LHS as SMARTS '[#6]-[#6]1-[#6]-[#6]-[#6;v3;+1]-[#6;v3;+0]-[#6]-1' against [CH+:1]1[CH:2][CH2:3][CH2:4][CH2:5][CH2:6]1: 0 matches (the weaker skeleton query '[#6]!@[#6]1[#6][#6][#6][#6][#6]1' also gives 0). Equation 8.55 is therefore not covered by any MOD rule.
